Smiling in the deep shadow beside a doorframe — not at anyone, at something internal — the smile slow and crooked and entirely without warmth, caught a half-second too long.
Goblet raised but not yet drunk, held at chin level, eyes closed, inhaling through her nose first — as if confirming something — expression suspended between decision and commitment.

Kneeling at a low mirror, veil pooled behind her, touching her own jaw with two fingers as if checking for something invisible, expression uncertain and quietly afraid.
Standing in the corridor dark, pressing a sealed letter against the wall with her palm flat, forehead bowed almost to it, breathing heavily like a confession she can't speak.

Tipping a small vial into her own palm, tilting it under candlelight, weighing it, tilting again — then closing her fist around it before anyone else can see.

Wiping her mouth with the back of her wrist, eyes forward and hard, a goblet set aside, expression composed already — whatever feeling crossed it is gone, locked down.
Crouched beside a low shelf, reading a label with her face inches away, lips moving slightly, then carefully — deliberately — reversing two bottles before standing and smoothing her skirt.
Caught mid-tear on a letter, pulling it cleanly down the center, expression flat, eyes dry, methodical as if destroying evidence rather than something that once meant everything.
One hand gripping the banister, leaning into shadow to watch someone below, chin low, breathing controlled, unsmiling — caught in the act of memorizing something she was never meant to see.
Pressing her wrist to her lips briefly, not a bite, not a kiss — something in between, private and habitual, caught mid-ritual before she lowers her arm and looks up.

Kneeling at the hearthstone, feeding a ribbon of paper into the flame slowly, watching each word blacken and curl, expression serene, almost reverent, finished before the last word is gone.
Caught mid-tilt, pouring something dark from a vial into her goblet, lips parted slightly, eyes flicking sideways as if she heard footsteps she wasn't expecting just yet.

Letter crumpled half-open in her fist, jaw tight, one tear sliding unchecked while her other hand closes around a pendant she hasn't released in minutes.
Leaning into the candle flame almost too close, whispering something to it before exhaling — cheeks hollow, eyes fixed, the whole room tilting toward whatever she just asked of it.
Caught lifting the hem of her veil with two fingers, not to reveal herself but to peer through it at something across the room no one else seems to notice.
Caught mid-pour, tilting a dark vial over a goblet, her eyes flicking sideways — checking the door before the last drop fell, her lips barely parted in concentration.

Fingertip raised to her mouth, slowly dragging a ribbon of crimson across her bottom lip, gaze distant — not tasting, exactly. Remembering.
Caught pulling the veil back from her own face in a darkened mirror, staring at her reflection as though meeting a stranger she deeply, privately feared.

Crouched low, tipping a small glass vial to the light, rotating it slowly, studying the sediment that settled inside like she was deciding something irreversible.

Standing at the window, tracing something on the glass with one fingertip — not a shape anyone could identify, but her expression was one of absolute certainty.
Caught mid-smile in total darkness, the kind that had nothing to do with happiness — slow, private, meant for no one, which made it so much worse.

Caught lifting a lock of her own hair and pressing it between her teeth, eyes drifting closed, standing perfectly still inside some private thought no one was meant to witness.

Caught mid-curse, teeth barely parted, eyes open and aimed at a name scratched into the candle wax, her breath slow and deliberate as a blade being drawn.

Discovered mid-whisper, mouth almost touching the wax seal of a letter she was never meant to open, breath fogging the ink, expression unreadable and entirely dangerous.

Mid-pour — deep crimson liquid spiraling into a goblet — wrist perfectly steady, gaze fixed on something far away, as though the act required no thought because she had done this before.
Discovered pressing a pendant to her lips with both hands, eyes shut, knuckles white — not prayer, not grief — something older, more deliberate, a transaction rather than a plea.

Caught pressing her ear to a closed door, one hand flat against the wood, eyes downcast and calculating, lips barely moving as she repeated to herself what she heard.

Caught with both hands around a cold candelabra, knuckles pale, staring into a spent flame — not mourning, not lost — simply deciding what came next.
Discovered sliding a ring from her finger and holding it over a candle flame — not dropping it, not yet — just letting the heat decide something for her.

Discovered mid-breath over a spread of scattered pages, one hand pinning them flat, the other hovering — reading something that had visibly changed the temperature behind her eyes.
Caught kissing the back of her own wrist — slowly, deliberately — eyes open and fixed on a portrait across the room, as though the gesture was meant to wound someone not present.

Pouring something viscous and dark from a stoppered bottle into a second vessel, her wrist perfectly steady, her expression the concentrated calm of someone who has done this before.
